title: Redwood + ZenithCloud marketplace integration - tech sync
summary: Partner integration sync to align on Redwood marketplace listing, reference architecture for ZenithCloud's managed offering, security requirements (SSO, KMS, audit logs), and pilot benchmarks. Decided next steps for checklist, demo environments, and a 6-week pilot scope.
action_items: Maya Chen - Share Redwood marketplace listing checklist and sample listing draft by 2027-01-15
Liam Ortega - Provide reference architecture diagram (VPC peering + private deployment options) and estimated infra cost range by 2027-01-20
Diego Martinez - Share current ZenithCloud onboarding playbook and network constraints by 2027-01-18
Priya Singh - Send SOC2 report and KMS requirements doc to Redwood by 2027-01-17
next_steps: Redwood to provide a staging demo listing for ZenithCloud to review
Schedule a joint engineering deep-dive for the private deployment network flow (w/ infra team)
Agree on pilot success metrics (latency p95, cost/unit, SSO user provisioning) and timeline
Exchange contact list for legal/compliance in case additional agreements needed
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-01-12
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam Ortega (Redwood SE), Anika Rao (Zenith), Diego Martinez (Zenith), Priya Singh (Zenith)

[00:00] Maya Chen: ok hi everyone thanks for joining on time, i think we have about an hour, we'll try to keep tight. i'm Maya, AE on the partner program, with liam who is our SE. want to kick off with quick rundowns and goals?
[00:22] Anika Rao: hi thanks, yes my goal today is to get alignment on the marketplace listing checklist and the reference arch for our managed integration, plus identify blockers on security and timelines.
[00:35] Liam Ortega: great, we'll cover listing requirements, the reference architecture for both marketplace-hosted offering vs private deployment, and then security / kms / sso bits.
[00:45] Diego Martinez: quick note — our infra team is concerned about VPC peering limitations in some regions, and latency to Redwood hosted endpoints. we want options for dedicated/private deployments.
[01:05] Priya Singh: and i'm here for security — we need to confirm SSO (SAML) support, KMS integration, audit logs, and data residency assurances for our enterprise customers.
[01:20] Maya Chen: perfect. quick agenda: 1) marketplace listing checklist, 2) reference architecture sketch, 3) security requirements, 4) pilot and benchmarks, 5) next steps. any additions?
[01:31] Anika Rao: sounds good. also GTM — co-marketing assets and listing timing, but we can treat that as separate follow-up.
[01:40] Liam Ortega: i'll start with listing items — there are mandatory fields we ask partners to provide: product description, logos, pricing model, supported deployment modes (hosted, dedicated, private), and an initial reference arch diagram. we also include a set of integration tests for validation.
[02:02] Diego Martinez: on pricing, zenith wants to show both managed & bring-your-own-license styles; will that be supported on Redwood marketplace?
[02:12] Maya Chen: yes, you can list multiple SKUs. we'll share the marketplace listing template. note there is a verification step where our marketplace team reviews the listing — typical turn around is 5-7 business days once we have artifacts.
[02:28] Anika Rao: ok please send the template.
[02:33] Liam Ortega: moving to reference architecture — two common patterns: 1) Redwood-hosted integration where calls go to Redwood's hosted API (multi-tenant) with optional org isolation; 2) Private/managed where Redwood Private runs in customer VPC or via a dedicated Redwood Dedicated pool. i'll share a diagram — high level: client app -> zenith control plane -> Redwood runtime (hosted/dedicated) -> model KV cache and external KMS for encryption at rest.
[03:05] Diego Martinez: can you show egress flow for private deployment? we need to avoid internet egress for some customers.
[03:12] Liam Ortega: yes for private option we support VPC peering / private link + on-prem package. in those cases there is no internet egress for inference; keys stay in your KMS; we can also integrate with your HSM if needed. (note: transcription may read KMS as K M S or K N S sometimes)
[03:40] Priya Singh: on KMS — do you support customer-managed KMS across both hosted and private? and do you provide envelope encryption?
[03:47] Liam Ortega: for private and dedicated, yes you can supply customer-managed KMS (we support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault, and some HSMs). for hosted, we have an option for customer-managed keys for enterprise plans but there are network constraints; we'll include specifics in the security doc.
[04:05] Anika Rao: any caveats about KV cache and caching of prefixes — our legal team asks about data retention and whether cached prompts could be exposed.
[04:18] Maya Chen: good question — Redwood's caching is optional per-route. for partner listings we recommend disabling prefix caching for sensitive flows or using a per-customer cache partitioning. we'll capture recommended defaults in the ref arch doc.
[04:36] Diego Martinez: latency numbers — do you have typical p95 numbers for generation on a 2k token prompt for the curated open models?
[04:45] Liam Ortega: ballpark on our dedicated pools for a medium sized model, p95 is 400-600ms for token generation beyond first token — but it depends heavily on model, batch size, and sequence length. we'll run a benchmark for your specific workload (we should set expected prompt sizes).
[05:10] Priya Singh: speaking of benchmarks, we need reproducible tests in our staging environment. can we get a sandboxed account and a sample dataset?
[05:20] Maya Chen: yes we'll provision a sandbox staging listing and provide sample prompts and a benchmark harness — link to our benchmark spreadsheet will be shared.
[05:30] Anika Rao: for the listing, is there a place to show joint solution docs / reference arch? we want a 'reference architecture' tab on the marketplace listing.
[05:39] Maya Chen: yes, partners can supply a reference architecture PDF and a short 2-3 minute demo video. the listing UI supports attachments and linkouts to partner docs.
[05:50] Diego Martinez: network details again — can you support private link to our Azure region eu-west-2? we operate in a couple of eu regions and us-west.
[06:00] Liam Ortega: we have regions coverage for hosted; dedicated capacity can be provisioned in specific clouds/regions as part of a Reserved Capacity contract. private deployments can be done in your VPC in those regions; we'll note any quota constraints in the diagram.
[06:20] Anika Rao: security review — Priya, i'll hand off to you to list must-haves.
[06:26] Priya Singh: must-haves: SSO/SAML or OIDC for admin portal, RBAC for team-level access, audit logs exportable to our SIEM, SOC2 report, data residency (EU data must stay in EU), and ability to use our KMS. Also we need clarity on vulnerability scanning and patch cadence for on-prem packages.
[06:48] Liam Ortega: for SSO we support SAML & OIDC. RBAC is role-based with fine grained permissions in the console. Audit logs are available via streaming to your logging endpoint. For our on-prem bundles, we publish a security bulletin and a quarterly patch cadence; emergency patches can be pushed more frequently under enterprise agreements.
[07:12] Priya Singh: ok please share the security pack (SOC2, pentest summary, vuln policy).
[07:18] Maya Chen: we'll attach the security pack in the shared drive — expect that by Monday.
[07:23] Anika Rao: pilot scope — thinking a 6 week pilot with 2 production-like tenants, target metrics: p95 latency < 700ms for our mid-size prompts, inference unit cost under $0.015 per token (ballpark), SSO enabled, and successful marketplace listing by week 6.
[07:45] Liam Ortega: that seems reasonable. we'll run an initial baseline test to validate p95 and cost. note: cost depends on batching, quantization, and model choice — we can recommend a quantized variant to lower unit cost.
[08:05] Diego Martinez: any blocking legal items for marketplace? sometimes marketplace terms require indemnity clauses.
[08:12] Maya Chen: marketplace terms are standard; we'll surface the legal checklist. if there are special requirements we can route to legal review.
[08:20] Anika Rao: on GTM, we'd like co-branded collateral and a joint blog. we'll sync marketing separately.
[08:27] Maya Chen: yes we'll loop in marketing after technical sign-off.
[08:32] Liam Ortega: quick note on rollout: we recommend canary first — list in marketplace but set the default offering to private/dedicated for enterprise customers, and then enable hosted listing for smaller customers. that avoids capacity surprises.
[08:48] Priya Singh: any extra compliance for EU? Data residency plus DPA addendum?
[08:53] Maya Chen: yes we have DPA templates and data processing addendums; we'll include EU-specific language and export controls if needed.
[09:05] Diego Martinez: curious about observability — can Redwood stream per-route traces and token-level cost breakdowns to our console?
[09:14] Liam Ortega: we have per-route tracing hooks, token-level cost breakdowns in Redwood Console, and can stream metrics to your monitoring system via prometheus or datadog exporter.
[09:30] Anika Rao: ok let's recap and assign next steps.
[09:35] Maya Chen: recap: we'll send marketplace checklist and sample listing, liam will provide ref-arch and estimated infra cost range, priya will get security docs from zenith, diego will send network constraints. pilot scope is 6 weeks — we'll draft pilot success metrics and share.
[09:52] Diego Martinez: timeline sounds good. can we get staging creds for the benchmark harness this week?
[09:58] Liam Ortega: yes i'll provision sandbox creds and the benchmark harness by end of week.
[10:05] Priya Singh: please route security docs to my email priya@zenithcloud.com, i'll review and flag any gaps.
[10:12] Maya Chen: perfect, i'll send meeting notes and action items after this. thanks everyone.
[10:20] Anika Rao: thanks, talk soon.
[10:24] meeting end

Notes: transcript contains occasional transcription errors (e.g., K V cache -> KV cache, some product names slightly off). References shared: marketplace listing template (link: https://redwood.ai/partners/marketplace-checklist), benchmark harness (link: https://redwood.ai/partners/benchmark), security pack (internal link to be shared).
file_notes: Transcription intentionally includes natural speech patterns, brief crosstalk, and minor mis-transcriptions common to Fireflies exports. Document saved under partners folder as partner technical integration sync artifact.
